oewn-01213509-n.learner: the act of giving someone hope or support
examples: Mr. Collins seemed neither in need of encouragement, nor inclined to be silent himself.
On such encouragement to ask, Elizabeth was forced to put it out of her power, by running away.

oewn-06704187-n.learner: words or acts that show you approve of something and are behind it
examples: If what I have hitherto said can appear to you in the form of encouragement, I know not how to express my refusal.
It was an encouragement of vice.

oewn-07556837-n.learner: the feeling you have when someone has given you hope or support
examples: She felt a rush of encouragement when she saw how well the plan was working.

oewn-00079373-r.learner: in a way that leaves no doubt; for certain
examples: Bingley likes your sister undoubtedly; but he may never do more than like her, if she does not help him on.
You think it a faithful portrait, undoubtedly.

oewn-01780648-v.learner: to not like someone or something, or to find them unpleasant
examples: that he should look at her because he disliked her was still more strange
"Let me write for you," said Jane, "if you dislike the trouble yourself."

oewn-08524579-n.learner: the place where something starts and first comes into being
examples: Every sentence of kindness was a fresh source of happiness to Jane.
In her own past behaviour, there was a constant source of vexation and regret.

oewn-06687867-n.learner: a paper, book, or organization that information is taken from
examples: The reporter checked every figure against an official source before printing it.

oewn-10225604-n.learner: a person who gives out information
examples: The paper refused to name the source who had told them about the meeting.

oewn-03059655-n.learner: a carriage that four horses pull, with one driver
examples: they were summoned by the arrival of the coach
I thought we never should have got into the coach.

oewn-09951098-n.learner: someone whose job is to train a sports player or a sports team
examples: The coach made the whole team run laps before every practice.

oewn-02927500-n.learner: a vehicle that carries a lot of passengers and is used for public transport
examples: We took the coach from London to Bath because the train was full.

oewn-00820635-v.learner: to be forceful or firm about something and refuse to give way
examples: "Now, I do insist upon it, that you, all of you, hold your tongues"
"At once to insist upon having such a report universally contradicted."

oewn-00718950-v.learner: to state something firmly as being true
examples: He insisted that he had never seen the letter before that morning.

oewn-00779976-v.learner: to ask for something again and again in a pressing way
examples: She insisted and insisted until her father at last agreed to let her go.

connotation.why: chosen over plain 'ask' for pressing, repeated asking

oewn-07080699-n.learner: the way of expressing things in words, art, music and so on that belongs to one person, group, or time
examples: "My style of writing is very different from yours."
There is something very pompous in his style.

oewn-04820120-n.learner: elegance that is stylish and marks a person out from others
examples: she had no conversation, no style, no taste, no beauty

connotation.why: credits its object with elegance where 'manner' would only describe

oewn-04936080-n.learner: the way in which something is done or happens
examples: She dealt with the whole problem in her own quiet style.

oewn-00210690-r.learner: with strong eager feeling and holding nothing back
examples: "That is capital," added her sister; and they both laughed heartily.
Elizabeth laughed heartily at this picture of herself

oewn-00221335-r.learner: in a warm and friendly way
examples: Elizabeth honestly and heartily expressed her delight in the prospect of their relationship.

oewn-07371988-n.learner: a change that makes something better; a step forward in how something develops
examples: Tell your sister I am delighted to hear of her improvement on the harp
while they were supported by their mother's indulgence, what chance could there be of improvement?

oewn-00249844-n.learner: the act of making something better
examples: she must yet add something more substantial in the improvement of her mind by extensive reading
the care and improvement of his dwelling, which he cannot be excused from making as comfortable as possible

oewn-14445583-n.learner: a state that is better than the state before it
examples: The new house was a great improvement on the cramped one they had left.

oewn-00074163-r.learner: mostly; more than in any other part
examples: Elizabeth was chiefly struck with his extraordinary deference for Lady Catherine
In town, I believe, he chiefly lived
